tagline: The US marine-mobility beachhead — Biscayne Bay density, year-round demand, and an all-electric gateway to the Bahamas.
summary: Miami is the densest marine-wealth corridor in the United States and Navier's natural US entry point. Biscayne Bay, the Miami River, Government Cut and the Fort Lauderdale canals form a continuous high-value waterway with year-round demand that does not collapse with hurricane season the way the islands do. It is simultaneously the US super-app/B2B-corporate proving ground identified and the physical jumping-off point to the Bahamas — Bimini is only ~48 nm, inside Pioneer II all-electric range, making Miami the origin of an all-electric US-to-international corridor.

use_cases.title: Biscayne Bay premium water tier
use_cases.body: An in-app Navier water option linking Brickell, PortMiami, Miami Beach, and Fisher Island — bypassing causeway and bridge gridlock.

use_cases.title: Brickell ↔ Fort Lauderdale executive commute
use_cases.body: A quiet, fast bay/coastal commute replacing the I-95 / Brightline last-mile for finance and marine-industry executives.

use_cases.title: Yachting-cluster day charter
use_cases.body: Premium foiling day-charter out of Ft Lauderdale / Miami Beach Marina — the unit-economics anchor.

use_cases.title: Miami ↔ Bimini all-electric gateway
use_cases.body: An all-electric international hop to Resorts World Bimini, replacing a rough 2-hr ferry or a seaplane seat.

journeys.name: Miami ↔ Bimini
journeys.today: ~2 hr ferry (Balearia) several days/wk, or a seaplane seat; weather-sensitive across the Gulf Stream.
journeys.with_navier: A quiet, stabilized all-electric ~90-min crossing — the headline 'electric boat clears international customs' corridor.

journeys.name: Miami ↔ Fisher Island
journeys.today: Resident ferry or private launch; no road access at all.
journeys.with_navier: On-demand premium electric shuttle for the most ferry-dependent affluent community in the US.

journeys.name: Miami ↔ Fort Lauderdale
journeys.today: 45–90 min on I-95 in traffic; Brightline + rideshare last mile.
journeys.with_navier: A reliable ~40-min coastal commute for the finance and marine-industry corridor.

journeys.name: Miami ↔ Nassau
journeys.today: 3.5-hr Balearia fast-ferry (seasonal) or a flight; the crossing is often rough.
journeys.with_navier: A comfortable Quanta-LR premium line-haul across the Florida Straits (H2 2026+).

journeys.name: Miami ↔ Key West
journeys.today: 3.5-hr drive down US-1 or a flight; the Key West Express runs from Ft Myers, not Miami.
journeys.with_navier: A direct Quanta-LR coastal run, or Pioneer II island-hops via Islamorada/Marathon.

journeys.name: South Beach ↔ Brickell (event-surge)
journeys.today: 25–45 min by car — and during Art Basel the MacArthur Causeway locks up, pushing the drive to 1.5–2 hours.
journeys.with_navier: An 11-minute foiling hop that holds at 11 minutes even when the causeways are gridlocked — turning peak-event congestion into Navier's strongest demand window.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the intra-bay and coastal layer: Biscayne Bay, Fisher Island, Miami↔Ft Lauderdale, and the marquee all-electric Miami↔Bimini international leg (~48 nm).
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) unlocks the Florida-Straits line-haul to Nassau (~150 nm) and the run to Key West (~130 nm) with no charging dependency.

competitive_landscape: Water taxis (Miami / Ft Lauderdale), Balearia fast-ferry to Bimini/Bahamas, and Tropic Ocean Airways seaplanes serve the corridor today — all demand evidence and potential partners. Heli charter is the premium air analog. Private center-console and superyacht charter fragment the leisure layer.
seasonality: Year-round demand on the bay/corporate side (a key advantage over the islands). Atlantic hurricane season (Jun–Nov, peak Aug–Oct) raises sea state on the Bimini/Nassau crossings; winter (Dec–Apr) is calmest and highest-tourism.
regulatory_note: US Coast Guard inspection regime (Subchapter T for small passenger vessels); CBP clearance for Bimini/Nassau international legs; Florida's clean-marina and manatee/no-wake zones favor zero-emission, low-wake operation in Biscayne Bay.
